question: to the Commission Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Catarina Vieira (Verts/ALE), Per Clausen (The Left), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Jan-Christoph Oetjen (Renew), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Hannah Neumann (Verts/ALE), Jana Toom (Renew), Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann (Renew), Damien Carême (The Left), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Katrin Langensiepen (Verts/ALE), Dainius Žalimas (Renew), Kathleen Van Brempt (S&D), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left), Alessandra Moretti (S&D), Pernando Barrena Arza (The Left) Subject:

On 21 April 2026, Euractiv reported1 that the Commission, the European External Action Service and selected Member States intend to host a Taliban delegation for discussions on the deportation of Afghan nationals. 1.

Does the Commission recognise the Taliban as the legitimate government of Afghanistan? If not, with what status or in what capacity will this delegation be received for discussions on the return of Afghan nationals?

Does the Commission consider the guiding principles for future engagement as established by the Council to be fulfilled, particularly with regard to respect for all human rights, including the full enjoyment of the rights of women and girls, as well as respect for the rule of law, freedom of speech and media freedom, with specific attention to human rights defenders? If not, what are the grounds for deviating from these guiding principles, and has the Council given its formal consent?

In the light of Parliament’s competence in the area of justice and home affairs under the Treaties, does the Commission intend to formally provide Parliament with full transparency regarding this meeting, including details of the participating Member States, the agenda and the outcomes?
https://www.euractiv.com/news/exclusive-brussels-to-host-taliban-in-talks-on-afghan-deportations/.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.8.2026) The Commission was asked by 20 Member States and Schengen associated countries in a letter signed by their Ministers in October 2025, to coordinate contacts on returns with the de facto authorities, to ensure a coherent European approach. Their focus is on the return of persons posing a threat to public order or national security. Returns to Afghanistan need to be addressed in a comprehensive and coordinated manner, bearing in mind the challenges arising from the acute humanitarian and human rights situation in Afghanistan. The Commission and Sweden, on behalf of interested Member States, co-chaired a technical-level meeting with representatives of the de facto authorities of Afghanistan responsible for return and readmission, following technical-level discussions in Kabul, in January 2026. The technicallevel meeting aimed to give Member States the opportunity to address practical aspects of the readmission process. 15 Member States participated in the meeting. Operational engagement with the de facto authorities is in line with the Council conclusions of 15 September 20211 and 20 March 20232. It does not constitute nor imply recognition, which remains conditioned upon progress on the EU’s established benchmarks, especially counterterrorism, inclusive governance and human rights, with particular concern for the rights of women and girls. The EU has strongly condemned the systemic violation of human rights. The Commission acts in full respect of the Council conclusions and of its international obligations and will continue its unwavering support to all persons concerned by those violations of human rights. Following a briefing by the Commission and the European External Action Service to the Coordinators of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE), the Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration held an exchange of views with the LIBE Committee on 14 July 2026 on all aspects of the technical-level meeting.
